_comment: One table, two runners. The scanner normalizes a URL twice — once in PHP
(Scanner_Controller::normalize_url) when discovering and re-queueing pages, and
once in JavaScript (scan-engine.js normalizeUrl) before the browser crawls them.
Where they disagree, the same page is captured under two keys and the server-side
rule is silently undone on the browser path.
That is not hypothetical. The PHP side stopped force-appending a trailing slash to
file-like paths without the client being updated, so on a /%postname%.html permalink
structure discover returned '/x.html' and the client crawled '/x.html/'.
SCOPE — read this before trusting the table. What is pinned here is the
TRAILING-SLASH rule and nothing else. The two implementations are NOT identical in
general, and these known divergences are deliberately absent rather than covered:
- the JS `new URL()` strips a default port (':443' on https), PHP keeps it;
- `new URL()` lowercases scheme and host, PHP passes them through;
- `new URL()` resolves dot segments ('/a/../b' -> '/b'), PHP does not;
- `new URL()` percent-encodes reserved characters, PHP does not.
None of those are reachable from the scanner's own discover output, which emits
lowercase absolute permalinks with no dot segments — which is why they were left
alone rather than forced into agreement. If a future change starts feeding this
path arbitrary URLs, they stop being theoretical and belong in the table.
Each runner asserts the same table against its own implementation, extracted from
the shipped source rather than reimplemented. Neither can be made green by editing
the other, and a change to one side alone turns its runner red.
Run: node --test tests/unit/js/scan-engine-normalize-parity.test.mjs
php tests/unit/test-url-normalization-parity-php.php

cases.why: An ordinary permalink is a directory and gets the trailing slash.
The /%postname%.html permalink structure — the exact shape the divergence broke. Must be left bare on BOTH sides.
Site root is already a directory.
An already-slashed path is idempotent — normalizing twice must not double the slash.
The deliberate leading-dot exclusion: a segment starting with a dot is NOT a file, so /.well-known stays a directory. Reproducing this is what stops a near-miss port from creating a third rule.
Only the LAST segment decides. A dot earlier in the path is not a file marker.
Dot in both a middle and the last segment — the last one wins.
The query string survives normalization on both sides.
The slash is appended to the PATH, not after the query.
A non-default port is preserved verbatim.
Port preserved on the slashed branch too.

A dotted slug is treated as a file by the heuristic on BOTH sides. This is the heuristic's known imprecision, not a parity bug — WordPress's sanitize_title_with_dashes strips dots from slugs, so a permalink cannot actually produce this shape. Pinned so the two implementations stay wrong together rather than differently.
